chapter: Cab Calloway, Lunceford, Hampton and Armstrong, 1941-45
title: How McRae came to replace Joe Thomas in Lunceford's band
summary: Lunceford's tenor Joe Thomas wanted time off, and Lunceford had tried several tenor players who couldn't play his hard book.

story.theme_name: Getting paid: wages, tips and leaving over money
story.community_name: Playing in Lionel Hampton's big band

else. What I'd like to do now is -- you decided to go with Jimmy Lunceford. You replaced Joe Thomas. How did that come about?
This was also that year, 1942, during the war.

During that time, Jimmy was out in the midwest and he wanted -- something had happened to one of his tenor -- Joe wanted to take off -- I think Joe Thomas' was in the undertaker business. I think that's what he (inaudible) in Kansas City.

And something came up that Joe wanted to go home a couple weeks. Meanwhile, they wanted to combine his vacation with business, you know, because his people was in the undertaker business there in Kansas City.
He wanted to go home and take care of some business.

So anyway, they tried out about -- they were travelling all around Lima, Ohio and Cleveland, Dayton, Detroit.
So when Jimmy was going into Akron, he had tried out about four or five tenor players in those different towns and none seemed to play his book.
But I could understand. Jimmy had one of the finest books -- band (inaudible). You know, he had a great music book.
That time Wilcox was writing, Sy Oliver (inaudible) things were there, you know, Sy Oliver (inaudible) writing and all that stuff.
And those arrangements were really hard. So anyway, Jimmy sent a telegram to New York to Shoebuck, (inaudible) he would call him (inaudible).
So he says -- told Chu Berry, (inaudible) he sent me out to Dayton, Ohio to probably come out and join his band for two weeks -- two months, you know.
